title: The 'Rich Person' Money Habits That Take 5 Minutes a Day
audience: 18-28 year olds, early career earners, money-awkward Gen Z
tone: High energy, relatable, slightly confrontational about bad habits, practical

concept.hook: I spent $400 a month on coffee and didn't realize I was poor until I did this 5-minute math.
concept.story_arc: Hook → Track fun spending → 24-hour rule → Name your savings → CTA

shots.prompt: Vertical. Person holding a large coffee cup, looking confused. Transition to phone screen showing spending tracker app. Numbers appearing: '$8 coffee x 50 days = $400/month.' Calculator icon. Coffee cup lowers slowly. Expression shifts from confusion to realization.
shots.camera: [Push in] From coffee cup to phone screen with the math
shots.narration: I spent 400 dollars a month on coffee. And I didn't realize I was slowly becoming broke until I did this five-minute math.
shots.sfx: Coffee cup on desk thunk, calculator beeps, realization sound

shots.prompt: Vertical infographic. Three rules appearing one by one. Rule 1: Piggy bank icon labeled 'TRACK YOUR FUN SPENDING — NOT YOUR BUDGET.' Red circle around 'fun spending'. Rule 2: Hourglass icon labeled '24-HOUR RULE.' '$50+ purchase? Wait one night.' Rule 3: Savings account icon labeled 'NAME YOUR SAVINGS.' 'Trip fund, upgrade fund — saving feels like progress, not sacrifice.' Each rule animates in with a satisfying pop.
shots.narration: Wealth isn't about how much you earn. It's about three daily behaviors. Rule one: track your fun spending — not your full budget. Awareness alone reduces it by 23 percent without restricting yourself. You don't need a spreadsheet. Just one number: how much you spent on non-essentials this week. Rule two: the 24-hour rule. Before any purchase over 50 dollars, wait one full night. Most impulse buys disappear by morning.
shots.sfx: App notification pings, piggy bank clink, checkmark sound

shots.prompt: Vertical split. Left: impulse buy scene — person buys expensive sneakers, guilt expression. Right: same $200 → investment app showing growing graph. Piggy bank → investment portfolio transition. Arrow labeled '23% reduced spending without restriction.' Chart showing growth over time.
shots.narration: Rule three: automate savings last. Save after expenses — not before. And name your savings account something exciting. 'Trip to Japan fund.' 'My first investment.' 'Weekend escape fund.' Saving feels like sacrifice when it's vague. It feels like progress when it has a name and a purpose. That's how wealthy people think about money.
shots.sfx: Money transfer swoosh, investment growth chime

shots.prompt: Vertical direct to camera. Confident, energetic, relatable. Coffee shop background. Person smiles, delivers final line with energy. Follow button animation. Comment CTA.
shots.camera: [Static vertical] Direct to camera, high energy
shots.narration: Five minutes a day on your finances equals five hours a year of clarity. Your future self will thank you. Drop a 'CLARITY' in the comments. Follow for weekly money breakdowns that actually apply to your life.

metadata.youtube_title: I Spent $400/Month on Coffee Without Realizing It (5-Minute Money Fix)
metadata.youtube_description:
I didn't know I was slowly going broke until I did this 5-minute math. Three daily money habits that wealthy people use — that take less than 5 minutes a day.

📌 What you'll learn:
- The 'fun spending tracker' method (awareness = 23% reduction without restriction)
- The 24-hour rule to eliminate impulse buys
- How to name your savings accounts to make saving feel like progress
- Why wealthy people think differently about money

💬 Drop 'CLARITY' in the comments.
